c.st: The Copyright Office Belongs in a Library
c.x:
You're right about the age of Snow White, but things aren't always that rosy for Disney.  When they made a film from Kipling's The Jungle Book, that book was 73 years old.  If Walt (who took strong personal interest in the project) felt comfortable making money by adapting a work that old to a new medium, why shouldn't I feel comfortable adapting his even older older works?

(Yes, this is a Tu Quoque argument)

c.st: A Common Lisp Bookshelf
c.x:
Though will mostly repeat what others have said, here it is:

ANSI Common Lisp from Paul Graham is also a good CL textbook. I bought it as a complement to Practical Common Lisp and it also has a nice quick reference at the end.

Having read both On Lisp and Let Over Lambda, of those, I would recommend On Lisp more because it has more practical applications of macros, LOL is much more esoteric/playful/abstract, and not everybody is into that sort of thing.
